summary: One chaining Line tool replaces Polyline in sketches with connected edges. Clicks chain connected lines, and the two segments that meet at a point share it; 3-point Arc in the drawing bar adds arcs to the chain. A click on the chain's start closes it. A double-click, Enter, the Finish button or the first Escape saves the completed segments open, without a zero-length segment, and Line stays active for the next chain. A double-click finishes however long after the previous click it comes, and places its point first, as a click would: it adds a line to that point or, while a 3-point Arc waits for its point on the arc, completes the arc through it. A double-click on the last point adds nothing, and one where the segment would be invalid reports why and adds nothing. The second press of a double-click is judged on release: held still, it finishes a chain with a completed segment; dragged, it draws like any drag; with nothing complete, it is an ordinary click, so two quick clicks close together draw a short line. A press is a click only once it completes, so a cancelled press, one that loses its pointer capture first, or a drag cannot begin a double-click. Once a click saves the chain, by closing it on its start or by a double-click finish, the next quick click there is spent and starts no new chain, whether or not the save has been accepted. A press made while drawing is paused, such as during that save, places nothing and keeps its trailing click, even when the save is accepted or rejected before its release. A tool change or a cancellation forgets the earlier clicks, including a spent one, and ends a press still held. A press whose snap lands exactly on the chain's last point adds nothing. Enter, Finish, Escape, a tool switch and Finish sketch place no point, so they save the completed segments and drop an unfinished arc. While the snap chooser waits for a choice, Finish, a double-click outside it, a tool switch, its letter shortcut and Finish sketch close the chooser and save the completed segments; Enter and Escape keep their chooser roles. The press that opens the chooser is not the first click of a double-click, on any path. A press, drag and release with nothing pending saves one line at once; during a chain a drag adds a segment, as in 0.0.772. With only a start placed, Escape discards it, and an Escape with nothing pending returns to Select. Arc, Rectangle, Circle and Slot follow the same rule wherever focus is: the first Escape discards their pending points and keeps the tool. While a chain with a completed segment is pending, the toolbar stays in view: choosing another tool, its letter shortcut or Finish sketch saves the chain open first, and a rejected save keeps Line and the chain for correction. An Escape during a chain's save leaves the tool once the save is accepted and never aborts it. P selects Line, whose shortcut reads L or P. The chain keeps Undo last and Backspace, Close profile and Close with line, Cancel drawing as the explicit discard, the Line and 3-point Arc segment modes, arrow keys, Space and Enter, the horizontal and vertical relations of 0.0.775, which the closing line never gets, the attachments of Create relations and the snap chooser, and construction mode, which is chosen before drawing. A chain is one edit and one undo step, prepared once when it is saved; nothing is solved while it is pending, and hovering over a long pending chain renders no graph rows and none of its drawn segments. Older profile sketches that keep closed profiles only, and Curves, keep their earlier rules: a profile sketch closes with Close profile, Enter or a click on its start, a Curve finishes with Finish curve, and Escape discards either drawing. The path tool id and the polyline drawing kind remain aliases.
warning: Potentially breaking for people and automation that drive the sketch canvas: two clicks with Line no longer save a line. The chain continues until it is finished with a double-click, Enter, Finish or Escape, or closed on its start. Enter while a 3-point Arc waits for its point on the arc saves the chain and drops that arc, where Polyline placed the point at the cursor; Space or a click still places it. Escape now saves the completed segments of a pending chain, where Polyline discarded them, and an Escape with nothing pending returns to Select. With focus outside the canvas, the first Escape discards a pending Arc, Rectangle, Circle or Slot and keeps the tool, where it also returned to Select before. The Polyline button is removed and P selects Line. Accessible names change: Finish polyline is now Finish chain, and the snap hints Close polyline and Polyline start are now Close chain and Chain start. The Finish button shows Finish. The canvas instructions, the keyboard help and the drawing error messages say chain or Line instead of polyline or Polyline. WebMCP tools, their arguments and results, the CAD schema and saved documents are unchanged. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output.

checklist.schema: No CAD schema change: a chain saves through the existing append-sketch-entities edit with the existing line, arc, coincident, point-on-line, point-on-curve, fixed-axis, horizontal and vertical kinds. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol change; the Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. A pending chain is a pending workflow, as a Polyline was, so agent mutations return WORKFLOW_OPEN until it is finished or cancelled. A chain saved by a tool switch, Finish sketch or Escape uses the same cancellable, source- and version-checked submission as Enter. A finish while the snap chooser is open closes the chooser first and saves the completed segments without the pending point. The next step runs only after acceptance, a rejection keeps the draft, and an Escape during the save never aborts it. WebMCP tools and their arguments are unchanged.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. Line replaces Polyline in sketches with connected edges; Curves and profile-only sketches keep their rules.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved documents open unchanged, and the drawing tool is not persisted.
checklist.verification: cadPathDrawing.test.ts checks that each chain segment continues from the previous end, that only a return to the start bounding an area closes it, that an open finish keeps the completed segments and drops a pending arc end, and undo and mode switches between segments. cadPathDraftGraph.test.ts checks that the segments meeting at a chain point share it. CadSketchPathDrawing.test.tsx checks that a double-click, Enter, Finish and Escape save the same chain and keep the tool, that a chain drawn from the keyboard alone saves on Escape, that a drag from idle saves one line while a tap and a drag from the tapped point continue a chain, that a lone start is discarded and a further Escape is left unhandled, that Arc, Rectangle, Circle and Slot discard on Escape, that a rejected save keeps the chain and the tool, that an Escape during a save leaves the tool only after acceptance without aborting it, that a profile-only sketch and a new Curve keep their explicit finish through a drag and a double-click, that a double-click after a pause on the last point or on empty space, or past the drag slop where guides snap back onto the last point, saves once without a zero-length segment, that Enter, Finish, Escape and a double-click on a pending arc's endpoint save the completed segments and drop the arc, and that a double-click away from that endpoint completes the arc through its point and saves the chain once, while one where the arc would be invalid reports why, adds nothing and saves the chain once, that a quick second pick beside the start with nothing complete adds its short segment, that once a closure on the start or a double-click finish has saved the chain the next quick click starts nothing, that a press ended by pointercancel or by lost capture before its release cannot begin a double-click, that a click whose capture ends after its release still can, that a press begun while a closure or an open finish saves places nothing and starts or saves no chain when the save is accepted or rejected before its release, after which a click starts a chain and a rejected chain still finishes, that a tool change or a cancellation forgets the click a chain save spent, and that a press held through either draws nothing. CadSketchCanvasPicking.test.tsx checks that a line dragged from idle onto an ambiguous end saves once its end is chosen, that Finish, a tool switch and a double-click while the snap chooser waits close it and save the completed segments without the pending point, that a quick press after Escape on the snap chooser, with Line idle, a chain pending or the chain's end held beside the targets, opens the chooser again instead of reading a double-click, that a click made before Space opened the chooser does not pair with a later press, that a quick drag after the press that dismissed the chooser adds its segments instead of finishing the chain, and keeps its guide, attachment, snap chooser and wobble cases with each chain finished explicitly. CadSketchCanvasRender.test.tsx checks that hovering over a pending chain of 31 lines and an arc renders no graph rows, draws no segment again and saves nothing. CadWorkbench.test.tsx checks that Escape from the canvas or anywhere saves a chain with shared joints as one undo step and a second Escape returns to Select, a lone start, Arc, Rectangle, Circle and Slot from anywhere, that Enter, Finish and a double-click build the same graph, horizontal and vertical guides on chain lines but none on the closing line, that a chain drawn in construction mode saves construction edges, that a double-click on the chain start whose closure is saved before the second press leaves Line idle and the sketch finishable, with no new chain started, that a tool switch, its shortcut and Finish sketch save the chain first while a rejected save keeps Line and the chain, and that with a dimension selected Escape saves a pending chain and keeps Line, the next Escape leaves the tool, and a dimension selected again in Select takes the following one. CadCurveWorkbench.test.tsx checks that a Curve keeps Finish curve, offers no open finish and discards on Escape. Each of these regression tests failed with its fix reverted, except the double-click after a pause on empty space, Finish and Escape while an arc waits, and the two double-clicks during a pending arc, which cover behaviour that already worked. The third review round's tests each failed with the canvas of the previous commit, and targeted mutations of the deferral to release, the finish only with something to finish, the cancellation and lost-capture clearing, the release completing the click and the spent double-click each fail at least one of them. The fourth round's eight canvas tests each failed with the canvas of the merge commit; a paused press that keeps no trailing click, or keeps the click history, and a tool or cancellation reset that keeps the held press, or keeps both the last click and its draft change, each fail at least one of them. Main's Escape line in place of the chain's fails eight canvas Escape tests. After the merge of 0.0.780, the full Vitest suite (556 files, 6439 tests), lint, ui:check, build and the release check pass. In Chromium, run one spec at a time, the new cad-sketch-line-chain test chains clicked lines to a double-click, saves a dragged line, saves on Escape and returns to Select on the next, discards a lone start, saves before a switch to Arc and undoes a chain in one step, and it, cad-sketch-constraints, cad-sketch-editing, cad-kernel, cad-sketch-context-editing, cad-sketch-dimension-points, cad-sketch-dimension-selection and cad-sketch-arc-trim pass on the final commit; cad-sketch-offset and cad-workflow passed before the first review fix. Hover P50 at 4x CPU in a production Chromium build, 60 rectangles and a pending 50-segment chain, after a warm-up run, two rounds of three runs: Line 36.7 to 44.9 ms against 36.9 to 48.7 ms for Polyline on 0.0.779, P95 69.2 to 79.1 ms against 61.8 to 79.8 ms, the same within noise. Both are above the earlier 26 ms baseline, which had no pending chain; a pending 50-segment Polyline costs the same on 0.0.779, so Line adds nothing to it.

publicNotes.summary: Line draws connected chains and replaces Polyline.
changes: Line chains connected lines and arcs that share each joint. Click each point, then double-click, press Enter, choose Finish or press Escape to save the chain, or click its start to close it.
Press, drag and release with nothing pending to draw and save one line.

Escape saves a pending chain. With only a start placed it discards it, and with nothing pending it returns to Select. Arc, Rectangle, Circle and Slot discard their pending points on the first Escape and keep the tool.
Choosing another tool or Finish sketch saves a pending chain first. P selects Line.
publicNotes.compatibility: No file, schema or tool change. Older profile sketches and Curves keep their drawing rules. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: Finish a line chain with a double-click, Enter, Finish or Escape: two clicks no longer save a line on their own. While an arc waits for its point on the arc, Space or a click places that point and a double-click places it and saves; Enter, Finish and Escape save without the arc. Automation that clicks Polyline or Finish polyline should use Line and Finish chain.
